architecture.pattern: Modular Multi-Agent Service with Single-Page Client Application
layers: Presentation Layer: React 18 SPA (Vite, Tailwind, Zustand)
API & Real-time Layer: Express.js HTTP REST + WebSocket Server
Multi-Agent AI Core: 5-Agent Architecture (ARIA, VEDA, SCOUT, SENTINEL, PATHWAY)
Persistence & ORM Layer: PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM (with Cloudinary / R2 blob storage)
Legacy Layer: FastAPI Python service under migration audit

agents.VEDA: Document & Vision Intelligence Agent (OCR, notice parsing, extraction)
agents.SCOUT: Scheme Discovery Engine (Government MSME subsidy matching)
agents.SENTINEL: Regulatory Horizon & Change Monitor (Crawler, deadline reminder cron jobs)
agents.PATHWAY: Action & Resolution Engine (Compliance penalty calculation, action plans)

conventions.rule: Express backend uses native ES6 modules ("type": "module" in package.json). All local module imports MUST include the explicit ".js" extension (e.g., `import db from "../db.js"`).
Follow MIGRATION_PLAN.md: All new feature development targets `complyos-backend-express` (Node.js/Prisma). The Python FastAPI backend (`complyos-backend`) is in deprecation/audit status.

Express database access must strictly use Prisma client via `complyos-backend-express/src/db.js`. Never bypass Prisma with raw unparameterized SQL strings. Run `npm run prisma:generate` after schema modifications.

React components are organized into `components/ui/` (stateless visual primitives), `components/agents/` (agent interaction drawers/cards), `components/aria/` (chat elements), and `components/layout/` (structural shells). All pages reside in `src/pages/` or `src/pages/ca/`.
Client-side global state utilizes Zustand stores located in `complyos-frontend/src/store/` (`authStore.js`, `businessStore.js`, `notificationStore.js`).

The 5 agents (ARIA: intake, VEDA: document OCR, SCOUT: MSME schemes, SENTINEL: horizon/crawling, PATHWAY: penalty resolution) have isolated modules in both frontend (`src/components/agents/`) and backend (`src/agents/`).
Express endpoints route unhandled errors through `middleware/errorHandler.js` returning structured JSON `{ success: false, error: "message" }`. Route handlers catch errors or pass to `next(err)`.
Never hardcode secrets, tokens, or private credentials. Reference variables exclusively via `process.env` (Node) or `os.getenv` / Pydantic `BaseSettings` (Python). Follow `.env.example` templates.

steps: 1. Locate or create a route file in `complyos-backend-express/src/routes/<domain>.js`.
2. Define the route handler with HTTP verb (e.g., `router.get("/my-endpoint", authMiddleware, async (req, res, next) => { ... })`).
3. If a new router file was created, import it in `complyos-backend-express/src/app.js` and mount it via `app.use("/api/<domain>", <domain>Routes)`.
4. If database queries are needed, import `prisma` from `../db.js`.
5. Add the corresponding frontend API client call in `complyos-frontend/src/services/api.js`.

change_guides.task: Add a UI Component or Page
steps: 1. For a reusable UI widget, create `complyos-frontend/src/components/ui/<ComponentName>.jsx`.
2. For a top-level route view, create `complyos-frontend/src/pages/<PageName>.jsx` (or `src/pages/ca/` for CA portal).
3. Register the new page route inside `complyos-frontend/src/App.jsx` within the appropriate `<Route>` wrapper (e.g. `<DashboardLayout>` for authenticated screens).
4. If linking in navigation, update `complyos-frontend/src/components/layout/Sidebar.jsx` or `CASidebar.jsx`.
1. Open `complyos-backend-express/prisma/schema.prisma`.
2. Add the new `model ModelName { id String @id @default(uuid()) ... }` with appropriate relations.
3. Run `npm run prisma:generate` inside `complyos-backend-express/`.
4. Apply migration using `npx prisma db push` or `npx prisma migrate dev --name <migration_name>`.
5. If seed data is required, update `complyos-backend-express/src/data/seed.js`.

change_guides.task: Add a Service or Agent Capability
steps: 1. If creating an external integration, add `complyos-backend-express/src/services/<serviceName>Service.js`.
2. Export async helper methods and handle service failures gracefully.
3. If adding or modifying multi-agent logic, edit the appropriate agent in `complyos-backend-express/src/agents/<agent>.js` (or `complyos-frontend/src/hooks/use<Agent>.js`).
4. Test the service using `tests/testSuite.js` or via a dedicated route.
1. Open `complyos-backend-express/tests/testSuite.js`.
2. Add a test function asserting endpoint response codes and data structures.
3. Run `npm test` inside `complyos-backend-express/` to execute.
